§ 2Content

Classification of Bodies

TypeDescription
Constitutional BodiesMentioned in Constitution under any article.
StatutoryCreated by a law.
Non-Statutory/ExecutivesCreated by any Executive resolution/Resolution of Government.

§ 3CONSTITUTIONAL BODIES

Election Commission of India (ECI)

  • Articles 324-329 (Part XV)
  • Permanent & Independent body
  • Administers the election to the LS, RS, LA, LC, President, VP, but not for Panchayat & Municipality elections.
  • Composition: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) + 2 Election Commissioners (as determined by the President)
  • Appointment: By President, Serves till the pleasure of the President.
  • Tenure: 6 years or until 65 years of age
  • Removal: By President, Similar to the removal procedure of a Supreme Court Judge (CEC), other ECs are removed by President on the advice of CEC.
  • Salary: Same as a Supreme Court Judge
  • Nature of functions: Administrative, Advisory, Quasi-judicial.
  • 1st CEC: Sukumar Sen
  • Originally it was a single-membered body.
  • It became a Multi-membered Commission since 1989
  • 61st Amendment of 1988 reduced the voting age from 21 years to 18 years.

Important Articles:

  • Article 324: Superintendence, direction and control of elections
  • Article 325: No person to be ineligible for inclusion in, or to claim to be included in a special, electoral roll on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex.
  • Article 326: Elections on the basis of adult suffrage, Representation of People Act.
  • Article 327: Powers of Parliament to make provisions with respect to elections to legislature.
  • Article 328: Power of Legislature of a State to make provisions with respect to elections to such legislature.
  • Article 329: Prohibits interference by courts in electoral matters.

Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)

  • Articles 315-323 (Part XIV)
  • Independent Constitutional body; known as "Watchdog of Merit System"
  • Composition: in discretion of the President
  • Qualification: ½ of members must have held Government office for 10 years
  • Term: 6 years or until 65 years of age
  • Recruitment: All India Services and Central Services
  • Removal by President if:
  • found insolvent
  • found holding any office of profit
  • having an infirmity of mind or body
  • Misbehaviour (as recommended by SC through an enquiry board)

Related Articles

  • Article 315: Public Service Commission for the Union and for the States
  • Article 316: Appointment and term of office of members.
  • Article 317: Removal and suspension of a member of PSC.
  • Article 318: To make regulations as to conditions of service of members and staff of the Commission.
  • Article 319: Prohibition as to the holding of office by members of commission on ceasing to be such members.
  • Article 320: Function of PSCs.
  • Article 321: Power to extend functions of PSCs.
  • Article 322: Expenses of PSCs.
  • Article 323: Reports of PSCs.

State Public Service Commission (SPSC)

  • Articles 315-323 (Part XIV)
  • Same structure as UPSC
  • Term: 6 years or until 62 years of age.
  • Qualification: ½ of members must have held Government office for 10 years
  • Recruitment: State Services
  • Appointed by: Governor of the State.
  • Removal: same as UPSC
Though UPSC and SPSC are constitutional bodies but Joint Public Service Commission is Statutory in nature.

Finance Commission (FC)

  • Article 280 - a Quasi-judicial body
  • Composition: Chairman + 4 Members (Constituted by President in every 5 years)
  • Constitution has authorised Parliament to determine the Qualifications of member of Financial Commission.
  • Qualifications:
  • Chairman – must be experienced in Public affairs.
  • Members – a judge of HC or Qualified to be appointed as a HC judge.
  • Special knowledge of finance and Accounts of government and Economics.
  • Experienced in Financial Matter and Administrations.
  • Members are eligible for reappointment.
  • 1st FC (1951): K. C. Neogy
  • 14th FC: Y.V. Reddy
  • 15th FC: N. K. Singh
  • 16th FC: Arvind Panagariya
  • Members: Ajay Narayan Jha, Annie George Mathew, Manoj Panda, Soumya Kanti Ghosh (Part-time)

Related Article:

  • Article 280: Defines Finance Commission.
  • Article 281: Submission of recommendations of FC.
It makes recommendation to the President on the Net Proceeds of taxes to be shared between Centre & State. (Not binding)

GST Council

  • Inserted via 101st CAA, 2016
  • Article 279A
  • Composition: Joint forum of Centre & State.
  • Chairperson: Union Finance Minister.
Union Revenue Secretary acts as the ex-officio Secretary to the Council.

National Commission for SCs & STs

  • SCs – Article 338
  • STs – Article 338A
  • Composition: Chairperson + Vice-Chairperson + 3 members
  • All members appointed by President.
  • Originally, Article 338 provided for a Special Officer for SCs and STs.
  • Later, the 65th CAA, 1990 replaced the Special Officer with a multi-member National Commission for SCs and STs under Article 338.
  • Finally, the 89th CAA, 2003 bifurcated it into 2 separate commissions:
  • National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) – Article 338
  • National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) – Article 338A

National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)

  • Established in: 1993
  • Article: 338B
  • Originally it was a statutory body.
  • Mandal Case, 1992: SC directed Central government to constitute a permanent statutory body for Backward Class.
102nd Amendment Act of 2018 conferred the constitutional status and added a new article 338B to the constitution.

Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities

  • Part XVII
  • Article 350B - Inserted via 7th Amendment Act, 1956
  • Appointed by: President
  • Article 350A: providing adequate facilities at primary level education in Mother tongue to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.

Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)

  • Part V, Chapter V, Article 148-151
  • Head of the Indian Audit & Accounts Department.
  • Appointed by: President
  • Term: 6 years or till 65 years of age
  • A Single-membered body,
  • Removal: Done in the same manner as that of SC Judge.
  • Known as: "Guardian of Public Purse"
  • B.R. Ambedkar's mentioned CAG as the "Most important officer under the Constitution"
  • He acts as a Guide and Philosopher to Public Accounts Committee.
  • He compiles and maintains the accounts of State government, not central government.
  • CAG related Articles:
  • Article 148: Office of Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), appointment, removal, salary and other conditions of service.
  • Article 149: Duties and powers of CAG.
  • Article 150: Form of accounts of the Union and of the States.
  • Article 151: Audit reports must be submitted to President.

Attorney General of India

  • Article 76
  • Highest Law Officer of India
  • Appointed by: President
  • Qualification: should be eligible to become a SC Judge.
  • Assisted by: Solicitor General (Not a constitutional body)

Advocate General of India

  • Article 165
  • Appointed by: Governor
  • Qualification: must be eligible for a HC Judge
  • Advices State Government in legal matters referred to him by the Governor.

§ 4STATUTORY/EXECUTIVE BODIES

National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)

  • Established under Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
  • Composition:
  • Chairperson (Retired CJI or SC Judge) + 5 full-time members
  • Appointed by: President (based on 6-membered committee recommendation)
  • Tenure: 3 years or 70 years of age.
  • Members are eligible for re-appointment after completing their current term
  • Also known as the "Watchdog of Human Rights"
  • Current Chairperson: Justice V. Ramasubramanian

State Human Rights Commission

  • Established under Protection of Human rights Act, 1993
  • Composition:
  • Chairperson (Retired Chief Justice or HC Judge) + 5 full-time members
  • Appointed by: Governor (based on 6-membered committee recommendation)
  • Removal by: President
  • Tenure: 3 years or 70 years of age.
  • Members are eligible for re-appointment after completing their current term

Chief Information Commission (CIC)

  • Established in 2005 under Right to Information Act, 2005
  • Tenure: 5 years or 65 years of age
  • Not eligible for Re-appointment under Central/State Government

Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)

  • Established: 1964 by Executive Resolution
  • Initial Status: Neither constitutional nor statutory.
  • Statutory Status granted in 2003
  • Recommended by: Santhanam Committee
  • Appointed & Removed by: President

Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)

  • Established: 1963 by Executive Resolution
  • Derive its power from Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.
  • It is an Executive body.
  • Recommended by: Santhanam Committee
